questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Dumplings around the world, especially one from Ghana
How to cook healthy food with less fat
The history of trade along the Silk Road between China and Turkey
Why British food is popular in Africa
questions.why: They talk about dumplings found all over the world and sample kenkey from Ghana.

questions.q: How does Beth describe a dumpling?
options: A kind of bread that is served with hot soup
A sweet cake filled with fruit
A small pie baked in the oven
A filling wrapped inside cooked dough
questions.why: She says they're basically dough envelopes with a filling inside.

questions.q: What do we know about where dumplings come from?
options: They were invented in 17th-century England
Nobody is sure, but one theory points to the Silk Road
They started in Ghana and spread to China
Historians agree they were first made in Italy as gnocchi
questions.why: The origins are a mystery, but one theory puts their birthplace along the Silk Road.

questions.q: According to Beth, why are dumplings popular in Ghana?
options: They are cheaper than rice
They are the only food that children in Ghana like
They add carbohydrates and soak up sauce
They can be cooked very quickly
questions.why: She says they're a favourite way of adding carbohydrates and soaking up sauce and juices.

questions.q: When did Kafui Adzah last eat kenkey?
options: That same afternoon
The previous weekend
On a trip to Ghana years ago
She has never tried it
questions.why: She says, “In fact I had kenkey this afternoon!”

questions.q: What does Kafui say kenkey is eaten with?
options: Butter and bread
Guinness gravy
Cabbage and pork, like the dumplings in China
Chilli sauce or a black sauce with fish and shrimps
questions.why: She mentions shito, a chilli sauce, and a black sauce with shrimps and fish.

questions.q: Why does Kafui mention people who do manual work?
options: Because they are the only people who know how to cook it properly
Because they sell most of the kenkey in Ghana
To show that kenkey keeps you full for a long time
To explain why kenkey is expensive
questions.why: She says it fills the tummy and it takes almost a whole day before you feel hungry again.

questions.q: Why does kenkey take a long time to make?
options: It has to be fried several times
The maize is soaked in water for a week
The dough must rest for a month
It is cooked slowly on top of a chicken or beef stew
questions.why: Beth says the maize needs to be soaked in water for a week.
